panel.summary: Design doc (and matching code/test comments) justify the batching design with an inaccurate example: `insertTable` is not a multi-change command
panel.evidence: notes.md:278 — "a command that dispatches several changes (e.g. `insertTable`) undoes in a single step"; note-sync.ts:58 repeats it ("a command that dispatches several, e.g. insertTable"), and notes-undo-integration.test.ts's header calls insertTable "one CodeMirror transaction carrying several changes". In packages/notes/src/view/commands.ts:176 `insertTable` issues a single `view.dispatch` with a single `changes: { from: pos, insert: table }`. Every note command (toggleWrap, toggleLink, insertTable) dispatches exactly one transaction, and the only multi-change one is the unwrap branch of toggleWrap (commands.ts:75). The canonical design record therefore documents a motivation the code does not exhibit; a reader can't tell whether ViewUpdate-level batching is actually needed or what it is protecting.
panel.finding_key: docs/design/notes/notes.md::design doc (and matching code/test comments) justify the batching design with an inaccurate example: `inserttable` is not a multi-change command

coderabbit.summary: Isolate the test-only undo-stack accessor from `canUndo()`.
coderabbit.detail: **Isolate the test-only undo-stack accessor from `canUndo()`.** `doc.getUndoStackForTest()` is already used by production stores, but `canUndo()` also reads it on toolbar state refresh. This mirrors the existing undo-floor pattern, but keep the call in the undo-floor helper only so production undo capability continues to use the public `doc.history.canUndo()` contract.
